# DataCoolie

> Multi-engine, multi-platform data pipeline framework for Python — metadata-driven, SQL/Python-capable, batch-first.

DataCoolie lets data engineering teams maintain canonical pipeline intent as
metadata (JSON / YAML / Excel / database / REST API) and execute it on Polars,
Spark, Fabric, Databricks, or AWS Glue through environment overlays and
target-specific runners. Version: 0.2.0.

## Key Features

- **Engine-unified**: Compatible pipeline intent runs on Polars and Spark via the `BaseEngine[DF]` contract
- **Cloud-agnostic**: Local, AWS, Microsoft Fabric, and Databricks adapters pair canonical metadata with environment-specific paths, catalogs, credentials, and runners
- **Metadata-driven**: Connections, dataflows, transforms, schema hints, partitions, and load strategies are declarative
- **Right-sized compute**: Choose Polars or Spark from workload size, managed runtime, table features, and downstream consumers
- **Batch-first**: append, overwrite/full_load, merge_upsert, merge_overwrite, and SCD Type 2 on supported lakehouse paths
- **Lakehouse-native**: First-class Delta Lake and Apache Iceberg through the shared `fmt` API where the selected engine, addressing mode, and optional dependencies support them
- **Plugin everything**: Engines, platforms, sources, destinations, transformers, secret resolvers are all entry-point plugins
- **Observable by default**: Structured ExecutionLogger/SystemLogger JSON Lines with bounded snapshots or batches
- **Repeatable replay**: Bounded chunks run sequentially, and an optional
  `save_watermark=True` persists reader observations without turning the saved
  watermark into a replay checkpoint
- **Visual companion**: DataCoolie Studio explores projects, metadata, assets, lineage, sources, and ETL monitoring in a local-first web UI

## When to Use DataCoolie

- Building ETL pipelines that must run on multiple engines (Polars locally, Spark in production)
- Teams that need cloud portability (Fabric ↔ Databricks ↔ AWS ↔ local)
- Projects where pipeline configuration should be declarative, not imperative code
- Replacing per-engine boilerplate with a single metadata-driven framework
- Data teams that want AI agents to scaffold, validate, and evolve pipelines

## Comparison with Other Tools

- **vs dbt**: DataCoolie is a Python ETL execution layer; dbt is SQL-first transforms. They complement each other.
- **vs Airflow/Prefect**: DataCoolie handles read→transform→write→watermark inside jobs. Airflow/Prefect orchestrate when jobs run. Use DataCoolie inside Airflow DAGs.
- **vs custom PySpark/Polars scripts**: DataCoolie replaces the boilerplate patterns you rewrite per-job with declarative metadata.

## Install

```bash
python -m pip install "datacoolie[cli,polars-delta]==0.2.0"
# or
python -m pip install "datacoolie[cli,spark-delta]==0.2.0"
```

Use the [installation guide](https://datacoolie.github.io/datacoolie/guide/getting-started/installation/)
for the matching source-wheel handoff when this version is not published.
Focused examples list their additional optional dependencies in their recipes.

- [Home](https://datacoolie.github.io/datacoolie/): Overview, value proposition, and quickstart
- [Introduction](https://datacoolie.github.io/datacoolie/introduction/): Product boundary, ecosystem, SQL/Python sources, and scale model
- [User Guide](https://datacoolie.github.io/datacoolie/guide/): Route from installation through metadata authoring, project preparation, runtime operations, and deployment
- [Getting started](https://datacoolie.github.io/datacoolie/guide/getting-started/): Installation, engine quickstarts, own-data onboarding, and multi-stage dataflows
- [Metadata guide](https://datacoolie.github.io/datacoolie/guide/metadata/): Author metadata from reusable connections through dataflows, with each case's configuration beside its explanation
- [Metadata providers](https://datacoolie.github.io/datacoolie/guide/providers/): Choose file, database, or API-backed metadata storage
- [Examples and templates](https://datacoolie.github.io/datacoolie/examples/): Single Markdown catalog for discovery, with direct `guide`, `source`, `raw`, `project-files` and `download` actions for known samples
- [Runner examples](https://datacoolie.github.io/datacoolie/examples/runners/): Local, Spark, Databricks, Fabric, AWS Glue, replay and maintenance entrypoints
- [Configuration examples](https://datacoolie.github.io/datacoolie/examples/configuration/): Provider construction, local Database/API fixtures, optional dependencies and runtime settings
- [Dataflow examples](https://datacoolie.github.io/datacoolie/examples/dataflows/): Artifact SQL, Python function and transform project recipes, output checks and adaptation
- [Operations examples](https://datacoolie.github.io/datacoolie/examples/operations/): Incremental project runs, bounded replay, recovery and state reuse
- [Project and CLI workflow](https://datacoolie.github.io/datacoolie/guide/cli/project/): `datacoolie.yml`, environment builds and functions packaging
- [DataCoolie Studio](https://datacoolie.github.io/datacoolie/studio/): Local-first visual workspace for metadata, lineage, assets, sources, and ETL monitoring
- [DataCoolie Skills](https://datacoolie.github.io/datacoolie/introduction/ai-skills/): Official AI-assisted workflow for discovery, design, build, provisioning, and release
- [WWI Multi-Cloud Tutorial](https://datacoolie.github.io/datacoolie/examples/wwi-medallion-multicloud/): English and Vietnamese video walkthrough across local, AWS Glue, Fabric, and Databricks
- [Concepts](https://datacoolie.github.io/datacoolie/reference/concepts/): Architecture, engines, platforms, metadata model, orchestration, logging, secrets, watermarks
- [CLI](https://datacoolie.github.io/datacoolie/guide/cli/): Project initialization, validation, inspection, metadata conversion, and immutable multi-environment builds
- [CLI preparation walkthrough](https://datacoolie.github.io/datacoolie/guide/cli/quickstart/): Download the canonical artifact project, build it, and verify current/history scope
- [Runtime and operations](https://datacoolie.github.io/datacoolie/guide/operations/): Configure, execute, replay, maintain, observe, and troubleshoot runners
- [Platforms and deployment](https://datacoolie.github.io/datacoolie/guide/platforms/): Microsoft Fabric, Databricks, and AWS Glue deployment boundaries
- [Project](https://datacoolie.github.io/datacoolie/project/): Contributor workflow, tests, benchmark evidence and public decisions
- [Contributing](https://datacoolie.github.io/datacoolie/project/contributing/): Product-root setup, shared environment, docs checks and release verification
- [Testing strategy](https://datacoolie.github.io/datacoolie/project/testing/): Select affected tests and qualification cells; interpret skipped or unverified results
- [Expected-failure scenarios](https://datacoolie.github.io/datacoolie/project/expected-failure-scenarios/): Run a negative scenario and distinguish child failure from successful scenario validation
- [Benchmark reproduction](https://datacoolie.github.io/datacoolie/project/benchmarks/): Prepare local workloads and check JSON statuses, workload equivalence and provenance
- [Reference](https://datacoolie.github.io/datacoolie/reference/): Authored metadata reference, plugin entry points, CLI, environment variables, full Python API
- [Runtime configuration reference](https://datacoolie.github.io/datacoolie/reference/runtime-configuration/): Driver sessions, replay and logging configuration
- [Core API](https://datacoolie.github.io/datacoolie/reference/api/core/): Hydrated models, constants and registry factories
- [Orchestration API](https://datacoolie.github.io/datacoolie/reference/api/orchestration/): Driver factory, execution and transformer activation hooks
- [Source API](https://datacoolie.github.io/datacoolie/reference/api/sources/): Reader contracts and bounded-read hooks
- [Destination API](https://datacoolie.github.io/datacoolie/reference/api/destinations/): Writer contracts, target resolution and window replacement
- [Transformer API](https://datacoolie.github.io/datacoolie/reference/api/transformers/): ColumnMapping and transform pipeline contracts
- [Engine API](https://datacoolie.github.io/datacoolie/reference/api/engines/): Engine operations and WindowSpec
- [Platform API](https://datacoolie.github.io/datacoolie/reference/api/platforms/): Platform I/O and native secret hooks
- [Metadata API](https://datacoolie.github.io/datacoolie/reference/api/metadata/): Provider lifecycle and query-reference classification
- [Logging API](https://datacoolie.github.io/datacoolie/reference/api/logging/): Logger lifecycle and persisted record identity
- [Extensions](https://datacoolie.github.io/datacoolie/extensions/): Extension selection, activation, capability limits and discovery troubleshooting
- [Transformer plugin tutorial](https://datacoolie.github.io/datacoolie/extensions/transformer-tutorial/): Install the canonical package and verify masking, nulls and unconfigured output through a Driver
- [Source extensions](https://datacoolie.github.io/datacoolie/extensions/writing-a-source/): Reader hooks, watermark boundaries and metadata format limits
- [Destination extensions](https://datacoolie.github.io/datacoolie/extensions/writing-a-destination/): Writer hooks, bounded writes and backend capabilities
- [Transformer extensions](https://datacoolie.github.io/datacoolie/extensions/writing-a-transformer/): Constructor contract, Driver activation and pipeline ordering
- [Engine extensions](https://datacoolie.github.io/datacoolie/extensions/writing-an-engine/): Engine contracts and plugin-owned backend verification
- [Platform extensions](https://datacoolie.github.io/datacoolie/extensions/writing-a-platform/): Platform I/O contracts, entry points and shared runtime instance
- [Secret resolver extensions](https://datacoolie.github.io/datacoolie/extensions/writing-a-secret-resolver/): Prefix semantics, resolver construction and lifecycle
- [Metadata provider extensions](https://datacoolie.github.io/datacoolie/extensions/writing-a-metadata-provider/): Constructor injection, required hooks and startup lifecycle
- [Architecture decisions](https://datacoolie.github.io/datacoolie/project/decisions/): Public contracts and load-bearing choices
- [Blog](https://datacoolie.github.io/datacoolie/blog/): Engineering rationale and evidence notes

Start example retrieval from the published catalog, choose one entry, read its
guide and follow its explicit `source` or `raw` action. Multi-file projects
expose a `project-files` section in the catalog and one `download` archive; dirty
local previews identify themselves as unpublished and Skills must not guess
revisions or silently fall back to `main`.
